_readme: Team-owned valuation assumptions. Edit a value, then run `npm run data` in app/. Every number here is a choice we must be able to defend; data-driven inputs (revenue, consensus, free cash flow, price, shares, net cash) come from Bloomberg and are NOT set here.

priceOverride.why: Google Finance, NVDA, 24 Nov 2026 (price shown on the page). Leave null to use the Bloomberg DES price ($135.46, 20 Nov). On pitch morning, set today's price here and note the time, then run `npm run data`.

wacc.why: Damodaran, US semiconductor industry average cost of capital, January 2026: 10.55%. Team choice (24 Nov): the industry rate, argued on NVIDIA's net cash, margins and market position. Other estimates for NVIDIA are higher: Google Finance 14.45% (cost of equity 15%, beta 2.21, 24 Nov), Stock Analysis 16.42% (23 Nov), Bloomberg 19.3% (20 Nov). The sensitivity table and slides show all of them. To use another rate, put a number here, or "bloomberg" for Bloomberg's own 19.3%.

terminalGrowth.why: Long-run growth after FY32 (%), roughly nominal world GDP growth.

fcfMarginYears.why: Base free-cash-flow margin = average of these actual years (Bloomberg).

base.label: Base: analysts are right, then growth slows
base.why: FY28 revenue = Bloomberg consensus. Growth then fades in a straight line to terminal growth by FY32.

bull.label: Bull: consensus, with fatter margins
bull.why: Same revenue path as base; free-cash-flow margin 5 points higher (software and networking mix).

bear.label: Bear: share loss and one soft year
bear.why: A realistic downside: the build-out continues but custom chips and AMD take share, and customers digest their spending for a year (FY28 +10%, FY29 -5%, then recovery). Free-cash-flow margin 38.8% = NVIDIA's own FY27 year-to-date margin (docs/financials/AUDIT.md, Bloomberg), not an invented cut. Growth rates are the team's judgement, shaped like the FY23 pause and the FY20 dip.

stress.label: Stress: AI spending pauses
stress.why: The extreme case: FY28 revenue flat on FY27, then a 20% fall in FY29 as cloud companies cut spending, then slow growth. Margin 10 points lower from price competition. Harsher than anything in NVIDIA's history; shown as a stress test, not a forecast.
